text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak receives message from Jordan's King Hussein on ways to boost peace and discusses with Crown Prince Hassan efforts underway to save peace process.
- Prime Minister Ganzouri tells cotton holding companies to buy all of last year's store.
- Ganzouri conveys message from Mubarak to Lebanon's Hrawi ahead of meetings of joint Eygptian-Lebanese committee. Ganzouri says president is doing all he can for resumption of peace talks.
- Two Egyptian companies to build auxiliary bridges to run alongside Suez Canal bridge.
- Manpower Ministry to launch study on child labour to find best ways to protect affected children.
- Police arrest 14 terrorists, including a fugitive from the death sentence.
- Workers have dug 12 km (7.45 miles) of Sheikh Zaid canal.
- New adventure for Diana with Egyptian hero.

- Mufti says studying idea of launching Egyptian-Islamic satellite to help determine beginning of Moslem months, particulary Ramadan, so that months and festivals start at the same time in Arab and Moslem countries.
- Two brokerage firms suspended for two months for executing trades with prices that differed from actual prices on bourse.
- Food inspection authority in Alexandria holds 778 tonnes of Belgian meat awaiting decision from export officials. Meat had arrived in Egypt before supply minister slapped ban on Belgian beef.
